extracted.intended_audience: applicants, patent agents and national/regional patent Office examiners working with PCT international applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the international phase (filing, international search, written opinion, publication, supplementary search, optional international preliminary examination) and transition to national/regional phases under the Patent Cooperation Treaty.

rubrics_metrics.name: International phase and national (regional) phase division
rubrics_metrics.description: The PCT procedure comprises two main stages: the 'international phase' (from filing through search, written opinion, publication and optionally preliminary examination) and the 'national phase' (or regional phase) which leads to grant or refusal under national/regional law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During the international phase no national/regional Office may process or examine the application except at the applicant's specific request. National/regional Offices are not bound by results of international search/examination when examining in the national/regional phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of an international application (filing elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing includes a 'request' together with a description, one or more claims, one or more drawings (where required) and an abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'request' must include certain data such as applicant, inventor, any agent and formal details like title and priority claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receiving Office formalities and transmittal
rubrics_metrics.description: Receiving Office carries out procedural checks, accords an international filing date and sends copies of the application to the International Bureau (record copy) and to the International Searching Authority (search copy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transmission of the search copy occurs promptly once identification number allocated, formalities checks done and search fee paid; if translation is required, transmission follows payment/receipt of translation as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective of the international search
rubrics_metrics.description: The international search is to discover prior art relevant to whether the claimed invention is novel and involves an inventive step and to establish an international search report and a written opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search may not be required or meaningful where scope of claims uncertain, subject matter excluded, or multiple inventions claimed. Search normally performed at about 16 months from priority date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written opinion primary and secondary objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: The written opinion formulates a preliminary and non‑binding opinion on whether the claimed invention appears to be novel, to involve an inventive step and to be industrially applicable. Secondarily it identifies defects in form or contents and significant issues of clarity or support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The written opinion should be produced according to the same criteria used in international preliminary examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: International publication timing and content
rubrics_metrics.description: International publication of the application, the international search report and Article 19 amendments (if any) occurs at 18 months from the priority date; the written opinion and any informal applicant comments are made available at the same time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the search report is delayed it is published separately as soon as possible; written opinion may be translated into English in certain circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary international search option
rubrics_metrics.description: At the applicant's request, supplementary international searches may be requested from participating Authorities other than the main International Searching Authority, to extend the overall scope of the search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplementary searches may be requested from more than one Authority before 22 months from the priority date. Details, conditions, limits and time limits are set by each Authority and in Annex SISA of the PCT Applicant's Guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional international preliminary examination (demand)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may file a 'demand' for international preliminary examination in which the examiner further considers novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability, taking into account Article 19 or 34 amendments and applicant comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This leads to an international preliminary examination report ('international preliminary report on patentability (Chapter II)'). Using Chapter II has practical advantages for national processing but is not binding on national Offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: International preliminary report on patentability where no demand filed
rubrics_metrics.description: If no demand is filed, the International Bureau issues an 'international preliminary report on patentability (Chapter I)' on behalf of the International Searching Authority, containing the same content as the written opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 19 amendments are not taken into account in this Chapter I report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution of international-phase documents to designated/elected Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau distributes copies of the application, any amendments, any supplementary international search reports, and the international preliminary report on patentability (either the written opinion contents or the Chapter II report) to designated or elected Offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated/elected Offices receive these documents to assist national/regional examination; access may be allowed earlier where national law permits and applicant requested early processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: National (regional) phase entry timing (30-month rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: After 30 months from the priority date (20 months in certain States due to transitional provisions; States may set later dates), the application may begin its national or regional phase in each designated or elected Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National/regional Offices may not make further requirements beyond Treaty/Regulations for matters of form and content, but are not bound by international search/examination results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment and competence of International Authorities (ISA/IPEA)
rubrics_metrics.description: International Searching Authorities and International Preliminary Examining Authorities are national Offices or intergovernmental organizations appointed by the PCT Assembly and entrusted with tasks such as establishing international search and preliminary examination reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorities must meet appointment requirements and may be competent to act only for applications filed with particular receiving Offices according to notified decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant choice of Authority where multiple are competent
rubrics_metrics.description: Where more than one Authority might be competent to perform search or examination, the applicant chooses the desired Authority in the request or demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An Authority may offer supplementary search service even if it did not conduct the main international search.

rubrics_metrics.name: ISA responsibilities: classification and examiner assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: The ISA determines preliminary classification to identify whether other-field examiners are required and assigns the search to an examiner capable of meeting the time limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A definitive classification must be made by publication time. Notification of search copy receipt is sent using Form PCT/ISA/202.

rubrics_metrics.name: ISA consideration of unity of invention and additional search fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The ISA considers whether the application meets unity of invention and, if not, may invite the applicant to pay further search fees for other inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invitations may allow payment under protest together with a reasoned statement; a protest fee may be required for examining the protest.

rubrics_metrics.name: ISA assessment of excluded subject matter and when search need not be carried out
rubrics_metrics.description: ISA considers whether some or all subject matter is of the type the Authority is not required to search (e.g., excluded subject matter) or whether scope is so uncertain that a meaningful search cannot be conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If search not required or not meaningful, the Authority may declare that a search was not required or would not be meaningful.

rubrics_metrics.name: ISA use of earlier search results and refunds
rubrics_metrics.description: ISA determines whether to use results of any earlier search referred to by the applicant to establish the international search report and may authorize refunds accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules govern authorization of refunds if earlier searches are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: ISA invitation to provide sequence listing
rubrics_metrics.description: ISA may invite the applicant to provide a sequence listing if nucleotide/amino acid sequences are disclosed but no compliant sequence listing is included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence listing must comply with Administrative Instructions and be in an accepted language; see Rule 13ter and related paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: ISA duties regarding abstract and title
rubrics_metrics.description: ISA considers whether the abstract and title are appropriate and in certain circumstances may draft alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Rules and paragraphs referenced (e.g., Rule 43 and paragraphs 16.33–16.47).

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of international search report and written opinion (or declaration)
rubrics_metrics.description: ISA establishes a search report indicating search results and a written opinion on novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability, or makes a declaration that a search was not required or would not be meaningful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These documents are transmitted to the International Bureau and applicant on the same day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for establishing ISR and written opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: The ISA must establish the international search report and written opinion within three months from receipt of the search copy or nine months from the priority date, whichever is later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to meet these limits may have procedural consequences; timing is critical for applicant options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant options after receipt of ISR and written opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt, applicant may (a) send informal comments to the International Bureau for public availability; (b) submit Article 19 claim amendments with explanation and basis; (c) request supplementary international searches; (d) request international preliminary examination (file a demand); (e) withdraw under Rule 90bis; or (f) take no further action in the international phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 19 amendments should be accompanied by a letter indicating differences and basis; supplementary searches must be requested before 22 months from priority date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality prior to publication
rubrics_metrics.description: All matter pertaining to the application is confidential prior to international publication and may not be accessed without applicant's authorization except for Treaty-specified transmissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated/elected Offices may allow access to communicated documents only as their national law provides and usually only after publication, unless early processing requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies of documents cited in search report available on request
rubrics_metrics.description: Within seven years of the international filing date, applicant or any designated Office may request copies of the documents cited in the search report, subject to payment for preparation and mailing if required by the Authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may sometimes be sent copies of citations automatically with the international search report.

rubrics_metrics.name: International-type searches for national applications
rubrics_metrics.description: An ISA may be entrusted with 'international-type searches' for national applications; these are similar to international searches but only the search is carried out (no written opinion unless specifically arranged).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 15(5) governs international-type searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing a demand: time limits and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: A demand for international preliminary examination must be filed within the later of (a) three months from transmittal of the international search report (or declaration) and written opinion, or (b) 22 months from the priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For transitional purposes to obtain a 30‑month phase benefit in certain States, a 19‑month limit may apply; applicants must check Gazette notifications and WIPO website.

rubrics_metrics.name: I P E A checking of demand and notification procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Preliminary Examining Authority checks competence, form, language and timeliness of the demand; if not competent it transmits demand to the International Bureau; if defects are present applicant invited to correct; late demand is considered not to have been made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If in order, Authority indicates date of receipt, transmits copy to the International Bureau and notifies the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents furnished to IPEA on receipt of demand
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau sends the IPEA a copy of the written opinion established by the ISA (unless same Office acted as both) and a copy of any Article 19 amendments and statements explaining amendments or impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the written opinion was not in a language accepted by the IPEA, the IPEA may request an English translation established within two months; applicant may comment on the translation's correctness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commencement conditions for international preliminary examination
rubrics_metrics.description: IPEA normally starts examination when it has: (i) the demand; (ii) handling and preliminary examination fees paid in full; (iii) any required translation under Rule 55.2; and (iv) either the international search report or declaration and the written opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions exist where Article 19 or 34 amendments are to be taken into account, or where applicant indicated postponement of examination; IPEA may delay start until amendments received or time limits expire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co‑incident search and examination when same Authority acts
rubrics_metrics.description: If the ISA and IPEA are the same Office/organization, international preliminary examination may start at the same time as the international search, unless the applicant requested postponement until after the Article 19 amendment time limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start is subject to possible need to invite applicant for copies of Article 34 amendments and to applicant's statement under Rule 53.9(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: IPEA assignment and preferred examiner continuity
rubrics_metrics.description: When examination begins the application is sent to an examiner responsible for the international preliminary examination. Where search and examination are by the same Office, the examiner who performed the international search should preferably perform the preliminary examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuity promotes consistent standards between search and examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top‑up search by IPEA
rubrics_metrics.description: IPEA carries out a top‑up search normally at the start of international preliminary examination to discover documents that became available after establishment of the international search report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No top‑up search is carried out if IPEA considers it would serve no useful purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to at least one written opinion during international preliminary examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant generally has the right to receive at least one written opinion directed to novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability prior to establishment of the international preliminary examination report, unless the Authority considers that (i) the invention appears to satisfy Article 33(1) criteria, (ii) the application complies with Treaty/Regulations checks, and (iii) the Authority does not intend to make other permitted observations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These conditions summarize Rule 66.1(e) and related provisions; the written opinion may be waived in limited circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of documents during preliminary examination
rubrics_metrics.description: IPEA takes into account the international search report, any supplementary international search report, all documents cited therein and any other documents considered relevant; it is not obliged to draw up a written opinion on claims for which no international search report was established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A supplementary search report received after the IPEA has begun a written opinion or examination report need not be taken into account.
